task.description:
WF-03 Step 4b -- HARD GATE on TEST-DESIGNER's regression coverage for ISS-0109.
Artefacts: test/specs/ISS-0109.md and test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs (14 tests),
covering test/support/tenant_fixture.ex. Gate-approved design: lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md (its FAIL-FIRST
PROVABILITY section enumerates cases C1..C6).

RE-DERIVE. Do not read TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary and agree with it -- this project's own
history is the argument for that: on the immediately preceding run (WF02-REQ066-20260820), the
TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gate caught a security test whose refutes were VACUOUS -- eight of ten
forbidden substrings were values the code under test could never observe, so every assertion was
trivially true against every possible implementation. It looked thorough and proved nothing.
Your job is to find that shape here if it exists.

FIVE THINGS THAT MOST NEED INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION:

1. TEST C1.2 -- THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. TEST-DESIGNER reports it runs the PRE-FIX fixture's entire
   oracle in-body (asserting {:ok, []} from replay_migrations/1 and that the table is still
   absent), then asserts the new assert_schema_complete!/2 raises naming the table -- i.e. it
   mechanically re-derives, in one test body, the fail-first proof that could not be obtained by
   checking out a pre-fix commit. Verify it actually does that, and specifically that the old
   oracle's assertion is a REAL assertion against the constructed broken state rather than a
   comment or a restatement. If C1.2 is sound, it is the strongest artefact this run produced;
   if it is theatre, the run's central claim is unproven and this is a FAIL.

2. THE CAPTURELOG WORKAROUND -- TEST-DESIGNER FLAGGED THIS ITSELF, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS THE
   HARDEST LOOK. ExUnit.CaptureLog cannot wrap the teardown line: it installs and removes its
   handler around a call in the test body, while the fixture's teardown runs from on_exit/1
   after the test process has exited. Test 11 therefore observes the line via a marker-filtered
   :logger handler installed and read from LIFO-ordered on_exit callbacks. VERIFY THIS IS NOT
   VACUOUS -- the question is not "does the test pass" but "WOULD IT FAIL IF THE LINE STOPPED
   BEING EMITTED, or if its marker/phase/schema_present_before_drop changed?" The strongest way
   to settle that is MUTATION: temporarily change or remove the teardown log line in
   test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, run test 11, confirm it goes red, then REVERT and confirm
   `git diff` on that file is empty. A handler-ordering trick that silently observes nothing
   would pass forever and assert nothing. (RELEASE-VALIDATOR proved two security criteria by
   exactly this method on the previous run; it is the only method that distinguishes a real
   test from one that merely looks like one.)

3. THE boolean() | nil DISTINCTION. The design was corrected mid-run so that `false` means
   observed-absent and `nil` means not-observed, because conflating them would break INV-F-10.
   TEST-DESIGNER reports asserting `nil` with an explicit `refute state.schema_present? == false`
   ALONGSIDE `assert ... == nil`, so the distinction itself is the property under test. Verify
   the nil case is genuinely REACHABLE by the construction used (an aborted transaction) --
   i.e. that the test really produces a not-observed field rather than an absent one. A test
   that believes it is asserting nil while actually constructing false would pass and prove the
   opposite of what it claims.

4. REVIEWER'S BINDING INSTRUCTION (step-03d ruling 3): the C6 oracle-rot test MUST read its
   observed set from capture_schema_state/1's `tables_present`, never from a raw
   information_schema.tables query (a raw read returns schema_migrations and would fail the
   unfiltered set equality spuriously). Verify by reading the test, and verify it genuinely
   fails in BOTH directions -- a manifest table missing from the oracle AND an oracle table
   missing from the manifest. A one-direction guard is a FAIL on this item.

5. COVERAGE COMPLETENESS against the design's C1..C6 plus the four extra requirements ORCH set
   in step-04's acceptance criteria (SS3.5 degradation rule on BOTH derived pairs; the INV-F-4
   absent-tenant negative case; the teardown line's closed-vocabulary phase pinned in both
   directions; no invented test for SS7.7). Name any criterion with no runnable test.

ALSO: independently re-measure the maximum test name length rather than trusting the reported
140. This repo has broken its own full suite FOUR times on ExUnit's 255-char limit (PR #351,
docs/anti-patterns.md) and the last validator to check this ran its own extractor rather than
accepting the number. Report YOUR measured maximum.

ALSO CONFIRM: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and both adopted modules are unmodified (both gates
passed them; a change would invalidate those verdicts), and no other fixture site was touched.

CONSTRAINTS: you gate, you do not rewrite the tests. On FAIL, name each gap per acceptance
criterion so rework is narrowly scoped. If you mutate anything to prove a point, REVERT IT and
show `git diff` is clean. Toolchain: plain `mix compile`/`mix test` only -- no
--warnings-as-errors, no `mix format` (ISS-0106 skew, filed, not yours). Postgres on
LETFLOW_DB_PORT from ./.env. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename, never
`git add -A`. handoffs/orchestrator.log is ORCH's -- leave it alone, and `git fetch` rather than
pulling if a rebase refuses.
acceptance_criteria: Test C1.2 is verified to genuinely execute the pre-fix oracle against the constructed broken state (a real assertion, not a comment or restatement) and then assert the new completeness check raises -- or is REFUTED as theatre

The teardown-line observation in test 11 is proven non-vacuous by MUTATION: the log line is temporarily changed or removed, test 11 is shown to go red, the mutation is reverted, and git diff on test/support/tenant_fixture.ex is shown clean
The nil (not-observed) case is verified REACHABLE by the construction used -- i.e. the test really produces a not-observed field rather than an observed-absent one
The C6 oracle-rot test is verified to read its observed set from capture_schema_state/1's tables_present rather than a raw information_schema.tables query, and to fail in BOTH directions
Coverage is checked case by case against the design's C1..C6 and ORCH's four extra step-04 criteria, naming any criterion with no runnable test
The maximum test name length is RE-MEASURED by the validator's own extractor and reported, not accepted from TEST-DESIGNER's number
test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and both adopted test modules are confirmed unmodified, and no other fixture site was touched
Any mutation performed for verification is reverted, with git diff shown clean
A single overall verdict (PASS or FAIL) is stated; on FAIL each gap is named per acceptance criterion

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS. Every acceptance criterion was re-derived from the artefacts themselves; TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary was not used as evidence. FOUR MUTATIONS were run against test/support/tenant_fixture.ex to separate real assertions from theatre, and all four were reverted (git diff on that path is empty and --exit-code returns 0).

1. TEST C1.2 -- SOUND, NOT THEATRE.
test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs:106 ("passes replay's old oracle and still fails the completeness check"). Read line by line: broken_state_tenant!/1 provisions with teardown: false and registers its own on_exit hard_cleanup, so the fixture's teardown can neither repair nor race the damage; promotion_assertion_runs is then dropped by raw SQL. The PRE-FIX oracle is then run as a REAL match assertion against that constructed state at line 114 -- assert {:ok, []} = TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations(tenant_id) -- executed code, not a comment and not a restatement, and strictly STRONGER than the pre-fix fixture's {:ok, _}. Line 115 then proves the state is still broken with a live catalog read: refute table_exists?(schema_name, @failure_14_table), an actual information_schema.tables query via Repo.query!. Only then does it assert the NEW oracle red: assert_raise ExUnit.AssertionError on assert_schema_complete!/1, with the message matched against both @failure_14_table and "tables_missing". That is a genuine one-body mechanical re-derivation of the fail-first proof: same database state, old oracle green, new oracle red. It is the strongest artefact of this run and it holds.

2. TEARDOWN-LINE OBSERVATION (test 11) -- PROVEN NON-VACUOUS BY MUTATION, TWICE.
MUTATION M1: the entire Logger.info call in log_teardown/3 (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:356-361) was replaced with :ok. Test 11 went RED -- "expected exactly one LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE phase=teardown line, got: []" -- raised from assert_teardown_line/1 at tenant_fixture_test.exs:475 through ExUnit.OnExitHandler.exec_callback/1 (Result: 0/1 passed, Failed: 1 test). That confirms both that the collector observes nothing once the line stops being emitted, AND that a failure inside an on_exit callback is genuinely reported as a test failure rather than swallowed.
MUTATION M2 (the subtler one): the line was KEPT but schema_present_before_drop=#{inspect(present)} was replaced with the constant schema_present_before_drop=maybe. Test 11 went RED again, this time on assert String.contains?(line, "schema_present_before_drop=true"), printing the full captured line as the argument. So the assertion binds to the line's CONTENT field by field, not merely to its existence.
The LIFO ordering is correct as written -- on_exit(assert_teardown_line) registered first therefore runs LAST, provisioned_tenant! registers the fixture teardown second, on_exit(install_collector) registered last therefore runs FIRST -- and M1/M2 empirically confirm the collector really is live across the fixture's teardown rather than silently observing nothing. NOT VACUOUS.

3. boolean() | nil DISTINCTION -- nil IS GENUINELY REACHABLE, PROVEN BY MUTATION.
The construction is capture_in_aborted_transaction/1 (test line 444): inside Repo.transaction it issues SELECT 1 FROM letflow_no_such_relation_iss0109, after which every further statement on that connection errors. Every per-field gatherer in do_capture/2 uses a raising call (Repo.query! / Repo.get_by) inside guarded/2, so each degrades independently.
MUTATION M3 changed ONLY the degraded value of the schema_present guard from nil to false -- schema_present = guarded(fn -> schema_present?(schema_name) end, false) -- and test 9 (tenant_fixture_test.exs:273) went RED with "left: false / right: nil". Decisive on two points: (a) the guard genuinely FIRES under the aborted transaction, because had the query succeeded the value would have been true, not the degraded constant; (b) the test binds to the degraded value, so it really is asserting not-observed and is not accidentally constructing observed-absent. The test additionally carries refute state.registration_present? == false and refute state.schema_present? == false alongside the == nil assertions, and pins both derived pairs at [] with length(expected_tenant_tables()) == 19 and length(manifest_versions) > 0, showing a naive derivation would have produced 19 and 31 rather than []. The false end of the distinction is independently pinned by test 3 (C2, dropped schema) and test 7 (absent tenant).

4. C6 ORACLE-ROT GUARD -- READS tables_present, FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, PROVEN BY MUTATION.
tenant_fixture_test.exs:374-396 obtains its observed set as state.tables_present from TenantFixture.capture_schema_state(tenant_id) at lines 382-384. There is NO raw information_schema.tables query anywhere in that test, so REVIEWER's step-03d ruling 3 is honoured; tables_in/1 rejects "schema_migrations", matching expected_tenant_tables/0's own exclusion, so unfiltered set equality is legitimate. Both directions are asserted (expected -- observed == [] and observed -- expected == []) and both were shown to actually fire:
MUTATION M4a: removed "variable_schemas" from @expected_tenant_tables -> RED with "a manifest migration created a table the oracle does not list: [\"variable_schemas\"]" at tenant_fixture_test.exs:393 (the observed -- expected direction).
MUTATION M4b: added a phantom table "letflow_iss0109_phantom_table" to the oracle -> RED with tables_missing=["letflow_iss0109_phantom_table"]. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: in this direction the test goes red slightly EARLIER, inside provisioned_tenant!/1's own assert_schema_complete!/2 call, rather than at the expected -- observed line. The direction is genuinely detected and the test genuinely fails, so this is NOT a gap -- but it is a double guard, not a single one, and worth knowing if that message is ever relied on. Both directions confirmed live.

5. COVERAGE, CASE BY CASE -- NO CRITERION WITHOUT A RUNNABLE TEST.
14 tests, all runnable; zero @tag of any kind, zero :skip, zero "TODO: implement test" in either the spec or the test file (grepped both). C1 -> tests 1-2; C2 -> tests 3-4 (test 4 is labelled characterization-only in BOTH the code comment and spec section 3, per design 7.2's warning, and is not dressed up as a regression assertion); C3 -> test 5; C4 -> tests 6-10; C5 -> tests 11-13; C6 -> test 14.
ORCH's four extra step-04 criteria: (a) the 3.5 degradation rule on BOTH derived pairs -> test 9 lines 291-293, present; (b) the INV-F-4 absent-tenant negative case -> test 7, asserting {:ok, state} with both present? flags false and no raise; (c) the teardown line's closed-vocabulary phase pinned in BOTH directions -> test 11 proves it IS emitted on the teardown path, tests 12 and 13 prove it is NOT emitted on the failure path or during a live test body; (d) no invented test for 7.7 -> confirmed, no test in the file asserts anything about the two modules' adoption, and spec section 2 states plainly that 7.7's evidence standard is behaviour-preservation rather than fail-first.

6. TEST-NAME LENGTH -- RE-MEASURED WITH MY OWN EXTRACTOR, NOT ACCEPTED.
An awk extractor over tenant_fixture_test.exs reconstructing ExUnit's actual atom form ("test " <> describe <> " " <> name) across all 14 tests gives MEASURED MAXIMUM = 140 characters / 141 bytes, on "test C4 -- capture_schema_state/1 failure boundary (design 3.5, INV-F-4) returns capture_failed only for a failure outside the field guards". Second and third are 137. That leaves 115 characters of headroom under ExUnit's 255-char limit. This independently confirms TEST-DESIGNER's reported 140; the extractor's count of names (14) matches the count of `test "` lines in the file, so nothing was missed.

7. NO OUT-OF-SCOPE MODIFICATION.
git show --stat fa7ad92 (TEST-DESIGNER's step-04 commit) touches exactly three paths: test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs (new), test/specs/ISS-0109.md (new), and its own handoff JSON. test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and both adopted modules (test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs) were last touched by step-03's commit 5556767 and are untouched by step-04, so the security and idiom gates' verdicts stand. No other fixture site is touched anywhere in main...HEAD.

8. MUTATIONS REVERTED.
All four mutations were applied to test/support/tenant_fixture.ex only, one at a time, each reverted from a byte-for-byte backup before the next. git diff test/support/tenant_fixture.ex produces empty output and git diff --exit-code on that path exits 0. The only file modified in the working tree afterwards is handoffs/orchestrator.log, which is ORCH's and was left untouched by this step.

EXECUTION EVIDENCE (mine, not quoted from step-04).
MIX_ENV=test mix compile succeeds (only the pre-existing lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex JoinCounter type warnings, unrelated to this run). mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs -> "Result: 14 passed" on the default seed, and again at --seed 424242 after the full revert -> "Result: 14 passed". Both adopted modules re-run together -> "Result: 20 passed". No hardcoded secrets or connection strings appear in either artefact; every broken state is constructed by real SQL against real Postgres (LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5472); nothing depends on wall-clock timing, concurrency, unseeded randomness, or on another test having run first (each damage-constructing test owns its own cleanup, and the module is async: false).

TWO MINOR OBSERVATIONS, NOT GATE FAILURES, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT LOST.
(i) Test 11 passes the expected tenant_id/schema_name to its trailing on_exit callback via :persistent_term, which is process-global. It is written and erased within the one module, the module is async: false, and the handler is removed in an `after` clause that runs unconditionally -- but if provisioned_tenant!/1 ever raised BEFORE the :persistent_term.put at line 337, the trailing callback would raise ArgumentError from :persistent_term.get and mask the real failure. Closing over the values would remove that mask.
(ii) C6's second direction is double-guarded, as described in item 4.
Neither blocks this gate.

issues.description: test 11 (C5 teardown line) passes its expected tenant_id/schema_name to the trailing on_exit callback through :persistent_term rather than closing over them. If provisioned_tenant!/1 raised before the :persistent_term.put at tenant_fixture_test.exs:337, the trailing callback would raise ArgumentError from :persistent_term.get and mask the real failure. Non-blocking; the values are available to close over directly.

C6's 'oracle lists a table the manifest does not create' direction is double-guarded: mutation M4b (a phantom table added to @expected_tenant_tables) turns the test red inside provisioned_tenant!/1's own assert_schema_complete!/2 call before the `expected -- observed == []` assertion at tenant_fixture_test.exs:389 is reached. The direction IS detected and the test does fail, so this is not a coverage gap, but the named failure message is not the one that fires.

result.next_action: PASS -- advance WF-03 to Step 5 (TEST-RUNNER) for the full suite. No rework to TEST-DESIGNER is required; the two MINORs recorded above are observations, not gaps, and no acceptance criterion depends on changing them.
